problems.title: Indices in a geometric progression
problems.question: Given b₁₄b₂₃=b₇b_k in a geometric progression, find the standard index k.
problems.idea: Apply the stated data to the relevant algebraic, counting, or geometric formula.
formulas: For bⱼ=b₁r^(j−1), the equality gives r³⁵=r^(k+5) after cancelling b₁².
steps: With positive r≠1, this forces35=k+5, k=30.
problems.answer: k=30 under the intended nonconstant positive-ratio assumption.
problems.note: The problem does not state that assumption. For a constant progression every k works; negative ratios or zero terms can also prevent a unique index. The general identity with k=30 always holds.

problems.title: Two cyclists change speed after meeting
problems.question: Cyclists from opposite ends meet after36 min. The first doubles speed, the second reduces speed10%; the first arrives6 min later. Find the first’s total time.
problems.idea: Apply the stated data to the relevant algebraic, counting, or geometric formula.
formulas: Let r=second initial speed/first initial speed. Their remaining times are 18r and 40/r minutes.
steps: The arrival condition is 18r−40/r=6, or 9r²−3r−20=0. The positive root is r=5/3.
The first’s post-meeting time is 30 min; total36+30=66 min.

problems.title: Opposite-sign roots of an exponential equation
problems.question: Find a for which(a−2)²2ˣ−(a−1)2^(−x)+2a−5=0 has two roots of different signs.
problems.idea: Apply the stated data to the relevant algebraic, counting, or geometric formula.
formulas: Put t=2ˣ>0. Multiplying by t gives g(t)=(a−2)²t²+(2a−5)t+1−a. Opposite-sign x-roots mean0<t₁<1<t₂.
steps: For an upward quadratic this requires g(0)>0 and g(1)<0. These give a<1 and a(a−3)<0.
Together0<a<1. Conversely these strict signs force two positive roots on opposite sides of 1, so they suffice.
